items.description: a sprint-1 stock row whose inventory_code is a full location-batch-serial code (e.g. "A12-B7-S001") has batch_number backfilled to segment 2 and serial_number to segment 3 after the up migration, and the row is still retrievable with its quantity and location intact

a sprint-1 stock row whose inventory_code has no batch/serial segment (e.g. "X-1" or bare "c") has batch_number and serial_number left NULL (not guessed or defaulted) after the up migration, and the row still survives and is retrievable
a stock row whose inventory_code leading segment differs from its canonical location keeps its location column unchanged after backfill; the code's leading segment never overwrites location

after the up migration the stock_records table no longer exposes a combined inventory_code column and batch_number/serial_number are first-class separately queryable columns (inspect migrated schema on the branch via the repository)

over a mixed set of the test's OWN seeded rows (marker-scoped SKUs, some conforming some nonconforming), the integrity probe reports the count of nonconforming rows (codes that could not be parsed into batch+serial) restricted to those seeded rows; assert the scoped/delta count, never an absolute whole-table total

for a row migrated up to first-class batch_number/serial_number with inventory_code dropped, running the down migration re-adds inventory_code and reconstructs its value from location + '-' + batch_number + '-' + serial_number, restoring the combined column

a single-step down-then-up round-trip (alembic downgrade -1 then upgrade head, never downgrade base) on this revision leaves the schema round-tripped: inventory_code re-added on down and batch_number/serial_number restored on up (mark @pytest.mark.migration, runs on an isolated ephemeral branch)

representative conforming and nonconforming rows seeded (idempotently, uuid-suffixed SKUs) BEFORE the up migration are all still present and retrievable afterward with quantity/sku/location intact and no row dropped, proving data survives the schema refactor (mark @pytest.mark.migration)

after the migration the UNIQUE(sku, location) constraint survives unchanged: inserting a second row with the same (sku, location) against the branch DB raises an IntegrityError, confirming the split neither dropped nor duplicated the key

batch_number and serial_number carry no NOT NULL constraint after the migration: inserting a row (uuid-suffixed SKU, idempotent seed) with NULL batch_number and NULL serial_number against the branch DB succeeds and persists

layering contract: the Alembic migration and the app/services parse+probe logic do not import the ORM session directly; the DB session/persistence is confined to app/repositories (the only ORM-touching layer)
